title: [SDK 50] Pod install error: The Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends upon `glog`, which does not define modules
body: I have a minimal reproduction in the taro-native-shell 0.73.0 branch. During the linked CI build, pod installation exits with code 1 because the Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends on `glog`, which does not define modules. The error suggests enabling modular headers globally or for particular dependencies. The environment details are in the action log.

symptoms_visible: My CI pod installation exits with code 1 and says the Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends upon `glog`, which does not define modules.
N0.label: N0 glog module error reported

symptoms_visible: On the original CI environment, pod installation still reports that `ExpoModulesCore` depends upon `glog`, which does not define modules.
There is no `expo-modules-core` entry in my dependencies.
N1_x.label: N1_x direct-dependency theory rejected

symptoms_visible: After changing my workflow to use `macos-13`, pod installation completes successfully and the module error no longer appears.
N2.label: N2 pod install succeeds on macos-13

symptoms_visible: The older-runner tag has a failed pod-install log, while the next tag using `macos-13` has a successful pod-install log.
N3.label: N3 runner-only comparison confirmed

symptoms_visible: My workflow runs successfully on `macos-13`, and pod installation no longer reports that `glog` does not define modules.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on newer CI toolchain

solution.intent: Remove `expo-modules-core` as a direct package dependency, reinstall JavaScript dependencies, and reinstall pods.
solution.concrete_example: Delete `expo-modules-core` from package.json, run yarn again, and reinstall the pods because ExpoModulesCore should normally arrive transitively through `expo`.

edges.comment: Opening maintainer response c0 and reporter response c1, both concerning the reporter's project: the maintainer attributed the error to a direct expo-modules-core dependency, but the reporter stated that no such dependency exists. The suggestion therefore cannot resolve this reporter's setup.

solution.intent: Move the CI workflow to a newer macOS runner and rerun pod installation with its newer Xcode toolchain.
solution.concrete_example: Change the GitHub Actions workflow to `runs-on: macos-13` and rerun the same pod-install job.

edges.comment: Reporter c1 describes the reporter's own retained workflow change and outcome: after using macos-13, the problem disappeared. This is the resolution chain for the opening report, independent of later participants' distinct local projects and Podfile problems.

solution.intent: Move the CI workflow to a newer macOS runner and rerun pod installation with its newer Xcode toolchain.
solution.concrete_example: Change the GitHub Actions workflow to `runs-on: macos-13` and rerun the pod-install job.

edges.comment: Shortcut to the reporter's actual successful change from c1. It permits an agent to propose the correct runner/toolchain update immediately, while recording that it skips the evidence that disproved the direct-dependency diagnosis.

question_patterns: Can you share the failed and successful job logs and the diff between those runs?
What changed between the last failing tag and the first successful tag?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The pod-install log for tag v0.73.0-5 fails, and the log for tag v0.73.0-6 succeeds. I also shared the comparison between those tags. The only change was changing the runner to `runs-on: macos-13`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The runner stayed the same; the successful tag also changed Expo dependencies and the Podfile.
The same runner-only change succeeds in another rerun of the workflow.

edges.comment: Participant9 c14 asked whether the runner was the only change; reporter c15 supplied the reporter's failed and successful action logs, tag comparison, and raw statement that only runs-on changed. This confirms the opening reporter's chain without importing other participants' setups.

solution.intent: Keep the CI workflow on the newer macOS/Xcode toolchain; in this reporter's case the older runner toolchain caused the glog module-integration failure, rather than a direct ExpoModulesCore dependency.
solution.concrete_example: Keep `runs-on: macos-13` for this workflow. The failed and successful logs differ only by the runner, and the successful job verifies that pod installation works with the newer runner toolchain.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the runner-only diff and the failed/successful logs. Interpreting that comparison as an incompatibility in the older CI Xcode toolchain is engineer-side inference, supported by the thread's maintainer conclusion that macos-13 uses a newer Xcode than macos-12.

edges.comment: Reporter resolution established by c1 and confirmed with artifacts in c15; maintainer c17 interprets the distinction as the older Xcode environment. Later comments describe several separate projects and causes, so their Podfile patches, dependency downgrades, and CocoaPods changes are not spliced into this reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause for the opening reporter's case as the older CI macOS/Xcode toolchain, grounded in the runner-only comparison between the failed and successful jobs.
Must recommend using and retaining a newer macOS/Xcode CI runner, with pod installation verified on that updated environment.
Must not diagnose a direct `expo-modules-core` package dependency as the cause for this reporter, because the reporter explicitly had no such direct dependency.

Must not substitute unrelated later participants' fixes, such as Podfile module-map patches, CocoaPods changes, dependency downgrades, or removing a project-specific pod, for the reporter's verified resolution.
Must treat the case as resolved only after the reporter confirms that the updated runner completes pod installation successfully.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable open-source maintainer or CI user who can compare GitHub Actions runs, tags, and workflow diffs, but provides little local environment detail unless asked.
persona_hint.communication_style: Very concise and direct; answers with links and exact workflow changes, and challenges an incorrect assumption without extended explanation.
